# Known Base addition successor

This successor-only fixture requires a separately observed, protected, engine-produced pure Base+MIR 5.0.20001 predecessor. The original instrumented `0C783` save is not directly admissible. The unchanged profile records this missing-input gate. No fixture, host test or supply model establishes a real startup-change event, native earning, save/cold result or reporter repair.

The synthetic provider adds two previously unpaid recipient recipes and retires only the checked plastic effect vector. All research counts, formulas, times, science ingredients and effects retain their existing contracts. The gear current work, queued plastic, detached saved work, three-force native bonuses, private/public carriers, new unpaid recipes and save/cold assertions remain the original case. The fixed source's old helper count was 1; its .42 current and .27 detached work become `.42*1/8000` and `.27*1/8000` fractions at the independently guarded normal level-1 count 8000 and map price 1. Separate research-unit comparisons use tolerance 1e-9, so a loose fraction tolerance cannot hide lost work. These are not preserved 42%/27% percentages or evidence of paid elapsed time/physical science consumption. The owner must also bind and compare the actual accepted pure-source frame.

The retained parent and normalization observer identify the foreign `mining` field as `manual_mining_speed_modifier` and `cannon` as `get_gun_speed_modifier("cannon-shell")`. The successor uses those same getters, alongside `worker_robots_battery_modifier`. The parent's zeros establish no zero baseline for the distinct mining-drill productivity or cannon damage getters; those unobserved extras may legitimately be nonzero and are not rewritten or assumed.

The test apparatus uses 64 normal-quality `mir-known-base-fast-lab` entities. Its data-only prototype clones the Base lab's exact seven science inputs, uses a void energy source, and changes only its own speed to 14400. At a 60-second research unit this is four science units per tick per lab before actual force speed/productivity modifiers. The source's actually observed clock remains exactly 16; no speed, research unit, earned level, bonus, queue or progress setter accelerates the case. Cloning all Base inputs also avoids narrowing MIR's available lab science during collection.

Each lab is stocked to 100 of each current research ingredient and refilled only when that ingredient reaches 16 or less. The observer reads only these named ingredients, without clearing inventories or merging their entire contents. It records starting stock, every inserted amount, refill ticks, actual research count/time/formula/science and observed force lab modifiers. Each ordinary completion must consume a positive amount of every required pack relative to that research's own supply ledger. Both event-time and settled consumption are recorded. Labs stop through portable `disabled_by_script` at completion; the next target starts only on a later tick, after the previous native debit settles. No leftover science is discarded. Final remaining stock is saved and compared again on each read-only cold.

The old one-time stock was only 6400 packs per ingredient, below the plastic level's nominal 16000 units at the preserved defaults. A focused host control gives even the old standard-lab apparatus the proposed speed and still reproduces starvation; the corrected threshold-refill apparatus completes that same normal workload in the model. The control also retains the ordinary/scripted, missing-consumption, wrong-target, unpaid-bonus, detached-progress, unrelated-state and cold opponents. This is a supply/cadence control, not an engine timing or lab result.

Before Root prepares or dispatches the target owner, the actual pure predecessor must provide measured force laboratory speed and productivity bonuses plus real current gear/plastic count, time, formula and science. If its normalization receipt omits lab productivity, that readback must be supplied explicitly; a host zero-modifier model is not authority. Root owns source normalization, exact package/profile/controller/875-setting bindings, native resource limits, two immutable cold reads and independent admission. F210, real third-party provider behavior, unknown reporter histories and stable acceptance remain outside this fixture's result scope.

The retained normalization observer is an old-501-only `__level__` control: it rejects an updated MIR version, additional mods and further configuration. Leaving it embedded in the target input will refuse before this successor can qualify the case. The owner needs a separately reviewed transition-input disposition, such as an owned copy that restores the original 48-byte Base freeplay control while preserving every native/script member and the original engine-produced protected source. This fixture is a newly added mod and supplies its own observer; changing the protected source in place or widening the old observer's authority is not an admissible shortcut.

The genuine target callback must still report `mod_startup_settings_changed=false`. All 875 effective startup values must also remain identical, including gate=true and inventory=false. Initial and cold markers expose the actual full dictionary, mods, clock and copied callback provenance; the owner compares these with the real pure-source receipt and exact transport binding. No fixture-owned settings declarations are added, and host events or Defaults cannot supply that evidence. The inherited tracked profile remains a historical missing-input definition with clock 1; Root's prospective selection must explicitly bind the accepted source and observed clock 16 before dispatch.

The control-stage observer uses a local recursive copy for its known plain snapshot, ingredient, mod and event tables. It does not depend on the data-stage `table.deepcopy` helper. Runtime host controls leave that global absent and check that captured event/ingredient tables and the protected initial frame remain independent through completion and cold readback. The original successor attempt's missing-helper refusal remains adverse evidence; this host correction alone establishes no native successor result.

During the declared lab phase on its research force, the observer separately records scripted completion notifications from exactly the eight signed plastic/LDS carriers already covered by its native carrier checks. Every such notification must report `by_script=true`; its name, script flag, force and tick appear in `scripted_carrier_events` on the initial and cold markers. These notifications never count as ordinary work or alter the lab cadence. Gear/plastic completions still require `by_script=false`, the declared order, actual science consumption and the full settled native frame. Ordinary carrier events, scripted main events and unknown events on that force still refuse with their exact event identity; the earlier event-filter refusal remains preserved.

The [accepted pure-source receipt](../../../spec/evidence/known-base501-normalization-independent-result-review-r01.json) and [destination receipt](../../../spec/evidence/known-base512-successor-independent-result-review-r01.json) now qualify their exact named scopes. The portable profile records sourceD38 and transition-copy1FD hashes, clock16 and the three-mod selection; it supplies no local save locator or launch authority. Original instrumental0C783 and the unfinished771cee4 plan remain preserved in Git/evidence. Host controls run through the canonical pinned-Lua driver; their inventory entry is not a native verdict.
